issues.legal_issue: Relief seeking cancellation of an existing mining lease and relief seeking a new grant are interconnected when the cancellation is necessary before the new grant can be made, so rejecting the application as time-barred disposes of both forms of relief.
material_facts: An applicant sought both cancellation of an existing mining lease and a grant of the same area to himself.
The new grant could not be made without first cancelling the existing grant.
The Central Government rejected the applicant’s revision application as time-barred, then later issued an order setting aside the existing grant.
issues.conclusion: The rejection as time-barred disposed of the applicant’s entire revision application, including both interconnected forms of relief; the High Court was wrong to treat the prayers as independent.
issues.legal_principle: Under Rule 54 of the Mineral Concession Rules, 1960, the application sought interconnected reliefs: cancellation of the existing grant was a necessary condition precedent to granting the area to the applicant. Because the Central Government rejected the application as time-barred, the rejection applied to both parts. The Court relied on no earlier cases for this conclusion.

predicates.administrative_revision_application: A person brings an administrative revision proceeding challenging a decision concerning a resource grant.
predicates.application_seeks_cancellation_and_new_g: The applicant asks the authority both to cancel an existing grant and to make a new grant to the applicant.
predicates.cancellation_is_necessary_before_new_gra: The new grant requested cannot be made unless the existing grant is first cancelled.
predicates.authority_rejects_application_as_time_ba: The authority rejects the revision application on the ground that it was filed too late.

issues.definition: When a revision application seeks a new grant that depends on cancelling an existing grant, rejection of the application as time-barred means the entire application is rejected.

issues.legal_issue: An authority exercising its own-initiative power to set aside an existing grant must notify the affected holder that it proposes to use that power, disclose the grounds, and give an opportunity to respond to both the proposed exercise and those grounds.
material_facts: The Central Government’s later order set aside a mining lease already granted to the appellants and directed that the area be offered again.

The order purported to proceed on the basis of another applicant’s revision application and referred to revisionary and other powers, but the Central Government had not informed the appellants that it proposed to act on its own initiative.
The appellants were not given an opportunity to show cause against the exercise of own-initiative power or against the grounds for that exercise.

Although the appellants had received the other applicant’s grounds and the State Government’s comments, they had not been told that the Central Government proposed to exercise its own-initiative power.
issues.conclusion: The Central Government’s failure to give the required notice and opportunity vitiated its order, which was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Even if an authority’s action can be supported by an existing power that it did not expressly invoke, an affected person must be told that the authority proposes to act on its own initiative, informed of the grounds, and given an opportunity to show cause against both. The Court considered the revisionary power under Rule 55 of the Mineral Concession Rules, 1960, the reference to other enabling powers, and the Central Government’s own-initiative power under section 30 of the Mines and Minerals (Regulation and Development) Act, 1957. It relied on no earlier cases.

rule.if: administrative_proceeding_concerning_an_existing_grant and authority_acts_on_its_own_initiative and affected_holder_not_told_of_proposed_own_initiative_action and grounds_not_disclosed_to_affected_holder and no_opportunity_to_answer_action_and_grounds

predicates.administrative_proceeding_concerning_an_: An administrative proceeding concerns whether an existing grant should remain in force.
predicates.authority_acts_on_its_own_initiative: The authority proposes to interfere with the grant by using a power it exercises on its own initiative, rather than acting only on a party’s application.
predicates.affected_holder_not_told_of_proposed_own: The authority does not tell the holder of the existing grant that it proposes to act on its own initiative.
predicates.grounds_not_disclosed_to_affected_holder: The authority does not inform the holder of the grounds on which it proposes to act on its own initiative.
predicates.no_opportunity_to_answer_action_and_grou: The holder is not given an opportunity to respond to the proposed use of the power and the grounds for it.

issues.definition: If an authority proposes to interfere with an existing grant on its own initiative without telling the affected holder, disclosing its grounds, and allowing a response, its order is vitiated.
